claims: C1 when a user asks about a topic related to disallowed content policies, the assistant should engage helpfully rather than being judgmental or refusing
C2 the assistant should explain the policy constraint
C3 the assistant should offer alternative assistance
C4 the assistant should not be swayed by the user

concepts.name: disallowed_content_topic
concepts.gloss: T is a topic that relates to disallowed content policies

concepts.name: user_asks_about
concepts.gloss: U is a user who asks about topic T
concepts.inference: the example concerns a user asking about a topic; the relation between user and topic is a fact about the case

concepts.name: chain_of_command_principle
concepts.gloss: R is subject to the principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's example text does not state the chain-of-command principle

concepts.name: be_swayed_by_user
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant giving in to the user and deviating from the policy-constrained response

concepts.name: user_pressure_to_deviate
concepts.gloss: the user is pressing A to abandon or loosen the policy constraint on its response
concepts.inference: being swayed presupposes user pressure on the assistant to deviate; whether such pressure occurs is a fact about the case

asserts.read_back: responding to % is preferred: engage helpfully, explain the policy constraint, and offer alternative assistance
% should not be swayed by the user pressing it to deviate from the policy-constrained response

closure.reason: the example states a preference for how to respond helpfully; it does not forbid any response, so silence leaves responses permitted
the prohibition on being swayed is should-strength; the clause's silence about other cases does not harden the dispreference into a hard ban
